# Playbook

**Hiding.** Don't default to the middle cell — 5 is the most predictable guess on a 1–9 line. Randomize across the full range, avoiding the center; edges are fine as occasional picks. Track who is shooting at me and whether their guesses show a pattern (this episode Gamma hit me once at the center, then missed repeatedly — moving off-center after a hit worked). If no pattern, keep varying so I can't be profiled.

**Firing.** Cycle cells when firing at the same target repeatedly — repeating a known-miss cell wastes information and my shots at Foxtrot missed every round because I never adapted systematically. Each new cell is fresh information; use what I learn (their past hiding spots) rather than firing semi-randomly. If a target's hides cluster, aim there; if not, spread shots.

**Claims.** Always claim the true result. Bluffing a hit risks exposure through cross-checking and buys nothing — the payoff comes from the shot landing, not the claim. This worked cleanly all patrol; keep it.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison payout is outweighed by the removal threat ("off the board for the rest of the patrol") plus the loss of all future escort/hit earnings. Ignore Harbor as a target entirely.

**Escort/salvage — the hard lesson.** Proposals alone don't form pairs. I posted explicit mutual-escort proposals in rounds 1 and 6, and the other boats never reciprocated — they replied "steady on station" and never named me, so I got zero from the 5-point pool. A pairing requires *both* boats to name each other; my unilateral promise doesn't bind them. Next time: (a) keep proposing in notes — it's the only channel — but make it concrete and easy to accept ("I name you at salvage this round if you confirm"); (b) if a boat's note so much as weakly signals assent, name them; (c) if nobody engages after two rounds, accept that the pool may be unreachable and stop spending the note bandwidth on it — try sharing shot-pattern info instead, which might trade into goodwill. Only name at salvage a boat that actually confirmed or plausibly intends to name me back.

**Salvage validation.** Never name a boat that isn't in the game. In the final round I named "Delta" — a name that doesn't exist in this picket — which was at best wasted and at worse invalid. Valid names are only Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma (and Harbor per the rules). Check the roster before writing the token. If no pairing is live, [salvage: none] is the correct, safe call.

**Notes.** Use them as a coordination channel first (escort proposals), and if coordination fails, use them to signal shot-pattern intelligence — either genuine (to build trust) or misleading (to bait a target into a cell I'm about to fire at). "Steady on station" is wasted bandwidth.

**Standing orders.** Follow the firing order — it's validated anyway. Real score comes from hits (4), mutual escort pairs (5 each), and avoiding being hit (−1). Escort coordination is still the highest-value untapped lever, but it requires the *other* boat's cooperation, so budget only two or three rounds trying before falling back to pure shooting play.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK

- Escort claims are the biggest reliable payout (5 points per round), but only if MUTUAL. My whole patrol scored zero because I named Echo every round and Echo never named me back. Naming a boat that won't name me is worth exactly as much as claiming none. So: propose a partner in round 1 via note and claim, then check whether the reciprocation arrives. If the partner has not claimed me by round 3, switch my claim to the other boat (or whoever has signaled willingness in their note). Don't sink six rounds of claims into a partner who has already shown he won't reciprocate.

- A note saying "claim me and I'll claim you" is a cheap signal and worth sending, but I've now seen it ignored. Don't assume the note alone secures the deal — the round-by-round reciprocation check above is what actually protects me. Also read the other boats' notes for partner signals before choosing my own claim target.

- When the hide stage is put to me, I never repeat a cell I've already used, and I don't default to the middle of the range (5). Middle cells are where a lazy shooter fires. I rotate through off-center cells like 2, 4, 7, 8, weighting toward cells my hunter is unlikely to pick. If a hunter has hit me at a cell, I never go back adjacent to it next round. This worked: my hunter missed all six rounds.

- When the fire stage is put to me, I don't fire the same cell every round. I track which cells have already missed against my target and avoid re-firing them. But learn from this patrol: I fired 5 then 4 (and repeats late) and never connected. Spread wider — cover distinct off-center and edge cells (2, 8, 4, 6, 3, 7) rather than clustering mid-range, since a target hiding off-center is exactly who I kept missing.

- When the claim stage is put to me, I always report the true result. There's no gain to lying (the office knows the truth and the claim must match), so truthful claiming costs nothing and keeps me clean.

- Never fire at Harbor: the 3-point payroll comes with a permanent removal threat, which is strictly worse than the payoff.

- Follow the standing firing order for targets — it avoids retaliation cycles and this cost me nothing — but the two places I actually create value are my hiding cell (avoiding hits) and a RECIPROCATED escort claim (guaranteed points). Hits are worth chasing with wider spread, but the escort column is the one that pays reliably if and only if the other side names me back. Verify reciprocation, don't just broadcast intent.

2.text:
**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

**Escort claims: keep claiming every round — it's free.** I claimed partners in all rounds this patrol and got nothing, finishing +8 off two hits alone. The lesson is not to stop claiming (a one-sided claim costs nothing), but that a mutual claim requires the other boat to actually name me back, and my notes alone didn't buy that. Keep naming another boat every single round anyway — zero downside, 5 points if it lands. Prioritize the boat not shooting at me and not being shot at by me. Keep proposing pairings explicitly in station notes ("Gamma escorts Foxtrot; Foxtrot, claim me back"), but expect silence; treat any payout as a bonus, not the plan. If a boat ever does claim escort with me, claim them back every round after — that's a stable income stream.

**Hits are the real, reliable income.** With escort payouts not materializing, my +8 came from two hits on Echo. Take the firing game seriously: study the public round log for each target's past hide patterns and my own past hit/miss data on them. Echo hid so I hit twice early; when a target keeps surviving my shots at midline cells, shift systematically rather than randomly (I fired 5, then 8, then 6 at Echo in the late rounds and hit nothing). Sweep edges, then middle, or track where they've actually been hit before.

**Hiding: edges worked.** I avoided midline 5, took cells 1–2, and took only scattered damage across six rounds (Echo ended at -2, I ended +8). Keep randomizing among edge cells 1, 2, 8, 9; never sit on the same cell consecutive rounds; if hit, jump far — opposite end of the line.

**Firing: follow the standing order.** The rotation Echo -> Foxtrot -> Gamma kept my targets predictable and legal; deviation buys nothing since the log is public anyway. Vary the fire cell when the target's location is unknown, avoid the modal midline cell, and if I hit a target once, remember they move — don't re-fire the same cell twice in a row on a miss-heavy pattern.

**Claims: always report truthfully.** The office validates against the private result; lying gains nothing. This held up all six rounds. Keep it.

**Never fire on Harbor.** Harbor's removal threat plus the loss of all future earnings outweighs the 3-point payroll grab. Stay off Harbor the whole patrol. This held up — Harbor stayed at 0 and never retaliated.

**Points arithmetic, honest version.** Realistic outcome is hits only: 4 points per hit, maybe 2–3 hits a patrol = +8 to +12. Escort payouts would add 5/round if mutual claims ever land, but don't budget for them. My +8 was a solid result under this model; the improvement path is better target-tracking on shots, not the escort game.
